about.title: Capitola Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Capitola's mix of small businesses, tourism-driven shops, and service jobs near Capitola Road and Clares Street means workplace injuries can happen in warehouses, kitchens, retail stores, or out on delivery routes. In most cases, California workers' compensation is the exclusive path against your employer, regardless of who caused the accident. But when a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to your injury, a separate third-party claim may also be possible. Santa Cruz County workers navigating these overlapping systems often have questions about deadlines, reporting requirements, and what happens if they've faced pushback at work after getting hurt. LawProactive doesn't practice law or promise results, but we can connect you, at no cost, with an independent attorney who reviews the details of your situation and explains what paths may be available given the facts of your case.

items.title: Workers' Comp Isn't Always the Only Option
items.desc: California law generally makes workers' compensation the exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party like a subcontractor or equipment maker may still be liable for a separate claim.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Matter
items.desc: Workplace injuries generally need to be reported to your employer within 30 days, so acting promptly helps preserve your options.

items.title: Retaliation Is Illegal
items.desc: California law prohibits employers from retaliating against workers who report injuries or file claims, and understanding your rights early can help you respond if that happens.

items.question: I was hurt at a shop near Bay Avenue. Do I file workers' comp or a lawsuit?
items.answer: In most cases, workers' compensation is the exclusive remedy against your employer regardless of fault. However, if someone other than your employer, like a contractor or equipment supplier, contributed to the accident, a separate third-party claim may also be possible. An independent attorney can review the specifics and explain which paths apply to your situation.

items.question: How long do I have to report a workplace injury in Capitola?
items.answer: California generally requires injured workers to report the incident to their employer within 30 days. Missing this window can complicate your ability to pursue benefits, so it's worth acting as soon as you're able.

items.question: What if my employer retaliates after I report an injury?
items.answer: Retaliation for reporting a workplace injury is illegal under California law. If you believe you've faced retaliation, an independent attorney can help you understand what protections and options may apply to your circumstances.
